input.strategy_title: Queue-aware GPU scheduling for distributed training workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Large training jobs fail or waste capacity because pods are admitted piecemeal:
a 16-GPU job can hold 12 GPUs for hours waiting for the last 4, starving other
teams, and partially scheduled jobs die on timeout. Customers running mixed
fleets also report that jobs land on suboptimal GPU topologies (crossing NVLink
domains) with significant throughput loss. We need admission and placement that
treats a multi-node training job as one unit and uses GPU topology where it
matters.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Multi-node training jobs are admitted all-or-nothing: no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Per-project GPU quota is enforced at admission time across training job types (PyTorchJob, RayJob). |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Users can see queue position, quota consumption, and admission state for their pending jobs in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Higher-priority workloads can preempt lower-priority ones according to an admin-defined policy. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Job placement can prefer GPU-topology-aligned nodes when the cluster exposes topology information. |

## Affected Components

- Distributed Workloads
- Training Operator
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- GPU sharing/fractioning (MIG, time-slicing policy management)
- Cross-cluster or multi-cluster queueing

## Open Questions

1. Do Kueue's current gang-admission semantics (waitForPodsReady) actually
   satisfy HLR-1 for PyTorchJob and RayJob at our target scale, or do we need
   scheduler-plugin work (e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue? The answer changes
   the shape of most implementation work.
2. Topology-aware placement (HLR-5) depends on node topology discovery that is
   only Tech Preview — is it mature enough to build on this release?
3. What preemption semantics do reference customers actually need — full
   eviction with requeue, or checkpoint-aware graceful preemption? We have
   conflicting field signals and no benchmark of checkpoint overhead.

# Enable Kueue all-or-nothing admission for PyTorchJob and RayJob

## Description

Branch A of the admission work, executed if the gang-admission validation investigation concludes that Kueue's existing all-or-nothing admission semantics (`waitForPodsReady`) satisfy the strategy's admission requirement at target scale: enable and configure those semantics for PyTorchJob and RayJob so a multi-node training job is admitted as a unit and never partially occupies GPUs while waiting for its remaining pods.

## Scope

- Enable and configure Kueue's all-or-nothing (gang) admission for PyTorchJob (via the Kueue integration) and RayJob (via KubeRay).
- Configure pod-readiness timeout and de-admission/requeue behavior so a job that cannot be fully admitted within its timeout releases everything it holds instead of dying partially scheduled.
- Validate admission behavior for multi-node GPU jobs at representative scale, including under competing load from other queues.
- Document the configuration and a rollback path to the previous admission behavior (this changes platform-wide admission semantics, so rollback must be tested).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A multi-node PyTorchJob or RayJob either has all of its pods admitted or holds no GPUs while pending.
- A job that cannot be fully admitted within its configured timeout is de-admitted and requeued without partial GPU occupation.
- Behavior is verified for both PyTorchJob and RayJob at representative multi-node scale.
- Rollback to the previous admission configuration is documented and verified.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (multi-node training jobs are admitted all-or-nothing: no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods).

# Provision coscheduling-based all-or-nothing admission for training jobs

## Description

Branch B of the admission work, executed if the gang-admission validation investigation concludes that Kueue's existing admission semantics do not satisfy the strategy's admission requirement at target scale: provision scheduler-plugin support (coscheduling) and integrate it with the queueing layer so multi-node training jobs are admitted as a unit. This branch spans scheduler-plugin enablement and queueing-layer integration; both are assigned to the Distributed Workloads component as the most relevant canonical component.

## Scope

- Provision and enable the coscheduling scheduler-plugin capability in the platform's scheduling path.
- Integrate the queueing layer's admission (Kueue) with the coscheduling behavior for PyTorchJob (via the Kueue integration) and RayJob (via KubeRay) so gangs are admitted and started atomically.
- Configure timeout and de-admission/requeue behavior so a job that cannot be fully scheduled releases everything it holds.
- Validate admission behavior for multi-node GPU jobs at representative scale, including under competing load from other queues.
- Document the provisioning and a rollback path to the previous admission behavior (this changes platform-wide scheduling behavior, so rollback must be tested).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The coscheduling capability is deployed and healthy in the scheduling path.
- A multi-node PyTorchJob or RayJob either has all of its pods scheduled and running or holds no GPUs while pending.
- A job that cannot be fully scheduled within its configured timeout is de-scheduled and requeued without partial GPU occupation.
- Behavior is verified for both PyTorchJob and RayJob at representative multi-node scale.
- Rollback to the previous scheduling configuration is documented and verified.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (multi-node training jobs are admitted all-or-nothing: no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods).

# Validate Kueue gang admission for multi-node training jobs

## Description

Resolves the strategy's first open question: whether Kueue's current all-or-nothing admission semantics (`waitForPodsReady`) actually satisfy the all-or-nothing admission requirement for PyTorchJob and RayJob at the platform's target scale, or whether scheduler-plugin work (e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue is required. The strategy states this answer changes the shape of most implementation work, so every downstream admission implementation is gated on this investigation's outcome.

## Scope

- Enumerate the concrete admission requirements from the strategy's all-or-nothing requirement (no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods; timeout death of partially scheduled jobs).
- Analyze the upstream and midstream Kueue all-or-nothing admission semantics for both PyTorchJob (via the Kueue integration) and RayJob (via KubeRay), including pod-readiness timeouts, requeue behavior, and de-admission of partial gangs.
- Exercise the semantics at representative scale on a test cluster (multi-node GPU jobs, e.g. 16-GPU jobs across mixed queues with competing load) and record failure modes: partial GPU occupation, starvation of other teams' jobs, timeout deaths.
- Produce a decision record selecting one of two bounded outcomes:
  - **Outcome A**: Kueue's existing admission semantics satisfy the requirement → the admission implementation is configuration/integration work.
  - **Outcome B**: Kueue alone is insufficient → scheduler-plugin (coscheduling) provisioning and integration is required.
- Enumerate which downstream implementation work changes under each outcome so the branch selection is traceable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written decision record exists that selects Outcome A or Outcome B with supporting evidence.
- For each of PyTorchJob and RayJob, the record demonstrates either (a) all-or-nothing admission holding at the tested scale, or (b) a documented, reproducible failure mode of partial occupation or timeout death.
- The record states the scale and load conditions under which the conclusion was reached.
- The record enumerates the downstream implementation work that changes under each outcome.

## HLR Traceability

- Informs HLR-1 (all-or-nothing admission of multi-node training jobs): this investigation does not implement HLR-1; it selects which conditional implementation branch delivers it.

# Determine required preemption semantics and checkpoint overhead

## Description

Resolves the strategy's third open question: what preemption semantics reference customers actually need — full eviction with requeue, or checkpoint-aware graceful preemption. Field signals are conflicting and no benchmark of checkpoint overhead exists. The answer determines the scope of the preemption implementation (an eviction-only policy configuration versus graceful preemption that coordinates job-side checkpointing, potentially including Training Operator changes for PyTorchJob).

## Scope

- Consolidate the conflicting field signals from reference customers into concrete preemption requirements (what is preempted, when, and what happens to the preempted job's progress).
- Define the candidate semantics: full eviction with requeue; checkpoint-aware graceful preemption; and whether both must be selectable by admin policy.
- Benchmark checkpoint overhead for representative distributed training jobs (checkpoint size, write time, resume time) so the graceful-preemption option is evaluated against data rather than assumption.
- Recommend the semantics to implement this release, with the evidence and the implications for job-side checkpoint coordination.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written recommendation exists that selects the preemption semantics to implement, traceable to consolidated customer input.
- Checkpoint overhead is measured for at least one representative multi-node training job, with the measurement setup documented.
- The recommendation states explicitly whether job-side checkpoint coordination (including any Training Operator involvement for PyTorchJob) is in scope for the preemption implementation.

## HLR Traceability

- Informs HLR-4 (higher-priority workloads preempt lower-priority ones according to an admin-defined policy): this investigation determines the semantics the preemption implementation must deliver.

## Notes

This investigation requires reference-customer input and a GPU-cluster benchmark; it is routed to a person rather than the AI investigation skill.

# Assess maturity of Tech Preview node topology discovery

## Description

Resolves the strategy's second open question: whether the node topology discovery capability — currently Tech Preview — is mature enough to build the topology-aware placement preference on this release. The answer decides whether the placement work exists now or is deferred, so the placement implementation is gated on this investigation with a removal outcome if the capability is not ready.

## Scope

- Document the Tech Preview scope, limitations, and known issues of node topology discovery from upstream and platform documentation.
- Evaluate those limitations against what the placement preference requires: preferring GPU-topology-aligned nodes (e.g. within NVLink domains) for multi-node training jobs when the cluster exposes topology information.
- Define pass/fail criteria for "mature enough to build on": completeness of topology information, stability of the API surface, and supportability of shipping a customer-visible feature on top of it.
- Recommend build-now or defer, with the consequences for the placement requirement documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written recommendation exists that selects build-now or defer, with the Tech Preview limitations enumerated and mapped against the placement requirement's needs.
- The pass/fail criteria used for the decision are stated explicitly in the recommendation.

## HLR Traceability

- Informs HLR-5 (job placement can prefer GPU-topology-aligned nodes when the cluster exposes topology information): this investigation decides whether the HLR-5 implementation proceeds this release or is deferred.

# Enforce per-project GPU quota at admission time for training jobs

## Description

Delivers the strategy's per-project GPU quota requirement: quota is enforced at admission time across training job types (PyTorchJob and RayJob), so a project whose GPU quota is exhausted has jobs waiting in the queue occupying no GPUs, using the platform's existing queueing-layer quota model.

## Scope

- Define per-project GPU quota enforcement in the queueing layer (Kueue ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model per the architecture context) covering both PyTorchJob and RayJob workloads.
- Ensure quota accounting reflects admitted workloads, so pending jobs neither consume quota nor hold GPUs.
- Ensure a workload that would exceed the project's quota is held pending until quota is available, uniformly across training job types.
- Document the quota configuration and a rollback path to the previous quota configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A training job submitted when its project's GPU quota is exhausted is not admitted and occupies no GPUs while pending.
- Quota enforcement behaves uniformly for PyTorchJob and RayJob.
- Quota consumption reflects admitted (not pending) workloads, and freed quota is reusable by newly admitted workloads.
- The rollback path to the previous quota configuration is documented and verified.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (per-project GPU quota is enforced at admission time across training job types).

# Admin-defined preemption policy for training workloads

## Description

Delivers the strategy's preemption requirement: higher-priority workloads can preempt lower-priority ones according to an admin-defined policy, implemented in the queueing layer. The semantics to implement (full eviction with requeue versus checkpoint-aware graceful preemption) are set by the preemption-semantics investigation that gates this epic.

## Scope

- Implement priority-based preemption in the queueing layer, configurable by administrators without code changes.
- Support the preemption semantics selected by the gating investigation (eviction with requeue, checkpoint-aware graceful preemption, or both as policy options); if graceful preemption is selected, include the job-side checkpoint coordination it requires, potentially spanning the Training Operator for PyTorchJob checkpointing.
- Ensure preemption interacts correctly with all-or-nothing admission: a preempted multi-node job releases its entire gang of GPUs (no stranded partial occupation) and is requeued.
- Document the policy configuration and its operational behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A higher-priority workload preempts lower-priority workloads per the configured admin policy.
- Preemption of a multi-node job releases all of its GPUs — no partial GPU occupation remains after preemption.
- The preempted job is requeued and, if the selected semantics include it, resumes from checkpoint.
- The preemption policy is administratively configurable without code changes.
- Preemption behavior is consistent with the all-or-nothing admission behavior delivered by the admission work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (higher-priority workloads can preempt lower-priority ones according to an admin-defined policy).

# Topology-aware placement preference for training jobs

## Description

Delivers the strategy's placement requirement: when the cluster exposes GPU topology information, job placement can prefer topology-aligned nodes (e.g. within NVLink domains) to avoid the cross-domain throughput loss reported on mixed fleets. This epic proceeds only if the topology-discovery maturity investigation concludes the Tech Preview capability is ready to build on.

## Scope

- Enable a placement preference for training jobs toward GPU-topology-aligned nodes in the queueing/scheduling layer, using the topology information the cluster exposes.
- Degrade gracefully when topology information is not available: scheduling behaves as it does today, with no failure or degraded admission.
- Validate placement outcomes for multi-node GPU jobs on topology-exposing nodes, including throughput comparison against unaligned placement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the cluster exposes topology information, multi-node training jobs are placed preferentially on topology-aligned nodes.
- When topology information is absent, job admission and scheduling behave as before this change.
- Placement alignment is demonstrable (job topology versus node topology) for at least one representative multi-node GPU job.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (job placement can prefer GPU-topology-aligned nodes when the cluster exposes topology information).
